canonical_claim: The Uncertain writer-duty transfer is implemented in PartWriteTxn::~PartWriteTxn, not enqueueWriterCleanupDuty; enqueueWriterCleanupDuty has no Uncertain branch and unconditionally builds and queues the duty.

CAS gtest suite renaming must change only the first argument of TEST, TEST_F, and TEST_P for colliding plain suites; all 62 production-symbol collisions are plain suites, while the two fixture suites do not collide and can be renamed with scoped whole-word edits.
The runtime proof is intentionally bounded to two runtime identities and one lane; it does not add unbounded retired-runtime history or change C++.
`CaRefDeltaIntakeCore` remains a pure downstream consumer of walk-plan key-set and fold semantics and does not own lifecycle protocol or fresh-cut provenance.
Snapshot codec fields and `RefLifecycle::Removed` are outside the Step 9 A/B catalog-cut slice and are owned by Step 9 slice C.

`CasRefWireVocab` and protocol contracts must not describe the retired snapshot-terminal surface; shared `RefTxnId` writer and validator helpers remain, and the retired namespace-cleanup marker and `Removed`-snapshot handshake are a zero-survivor audit target with no executable producer, consumer, DTO collection, or positive test in production.
The TLA+ model treats blocking joins as enabled-when conditions with weak fairness, proving absence of deadlock or livelock but not real-time join duration.

Probe A's two blind spots were a hole reproduced identically in both enumerations and a namespace dropped wholesale from one enumeration; the sampled Probe A mechanism was later superseded and deleted: `Gc::sampleRefListQuality`, `PoolConfig::gc_probe_a_period`, the `ref_list_probe` phase row, and all `CasGcProbeA*` counters were deleted, leaving one `cas/refs/` enumeration per fold round; Task T5 deleted Probe A rather than widening its witness rule.; The historical alternative of widening probe A was rejected; probe A is deleted outright rather than demoted or retained as a sampling mechanism.

The pre-CAS MergeTree disk-transaction contract was used as a batch of file operations rather than as one transaction for creating a logical part, allowing projections, clone/freeze, and mutable per-part files to use multiple independent transactions or per-file autocommit operations.

The non-CAS value of the transaction fixes is clarification of the `DataPartStorage`/`IDiskTransaction` responsibility boundary and removal of the implicit assumption that every sub-part can be safely committed independently.

Non-CA-gated changes to shared paths require separate upstream sign-off and regression coverage: `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` now commits each part's disk-storage transaction before the Keeper commit decision, the S3 client globally stops retrying HTTP 412, and the `ReadBufferFromFileView` fix changes the packed skip-index reader.

The `[TXN-ONE-PIPELINE]` refactoring removes patches caused by eager/deferred dispatch, the `moveDirectory` rename-window publish, read-your-writes gaps, and commit-position workarounds by introducing a `ContentAddressedDiskTransaction` and a two-phase `precommit`/`commit` contract.

Class-A patches are concentrated in `Disks/DiskObjectStorage/DiskObjectStorageTransaction.cpp` and `Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeData.cpp`; the remaining inventory is classified as legitimate CAS integration or independently removable code.

The dangling-precommit TLA+ gate adds constant `SabotageSkipParksDeadPrecommit` and liveness property `LiveDeadPrecommitReclaimed` to `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla`; the bug config must violate the property (a watermark-dead live precommit's manifest body stutters present forever under Skip) and the fix config must hold it.

The `RefCowMap` COW-overlay design for `RefTableState::committed` reuses the same immutable-base-plus-delta pattern Keeper already uses for `KeeperStorage::UncommittedState` (`Delta`/`applyDelta`/`rollback` over a committed `Container`), specialized to an ordered map.

In the `RefTableState` experiment matrix, E3 (transaction-layer instead of scratch copy) composes with E2 (COW owned-manifest index) or E4 (flat sorted-vector base) since a transaction layer works over either base, and E1 (relaxed replay) reduces the weight of what E2 must speed up; the comparison table is expected to judge combinations, not only single experiments.

The `FrontierUnproven::NoCatalogEntry` and `AppendAboveFrozenTail` buckets were removed outright (not retained with a comment) once they became unfireable-by-construction, because a zero-only bucket cannot change the invariant `sum(buckets) == frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`, and retaining a dead enumerator would falsely imply a live exit path to a reader.

`WalkTarget::frozen_tail` was deleted as an unread field (written at three `push_back` sites, read nowhere) once the frozen-tail break arm it supported was removed as dead code, since keeping the field with prose claiming it bounds the round would have been a false statement about the code.

The GC in-degree model replaced a bare integer refcount with a source-edge multiset (`+`/`-` deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)`); the fold computes net in-degree from the edge multiset, and the `BlobInDegreeMatchesActiveManifests` TLA+ invariant asserts the multiset exactly equals the active manifests referencing the blob, turning the `+`-not-yet-durable race into a pending-fold problem rather than a guard problem.; Mutable or persisted integer blob refcounts, including folding `prior_count + Σ ±1`, were rejected because a refolded removal can underflow the count, wedge GC with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and non-atomic folding under concurrent leaders could undercount; they were replaced by an idempotent source-edge set folded from append-only +/- journal records.

The attempt-scoped-generation fix moved all decision-bearing round artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/…` rather than the narrower original proposal of attempt-scoping only the four `gc/gen/<gen>/…` write-once artifacts, because `retired` is a writer-facing publish-gate input that `RetireView::refresh` LISTs and writers consult on the commit path, so a stale retired set from a deposed leader under its own `(round, fence_seq)` could otherwise influence live writers.

The B167 watermark models established that `build_seq` must be allocated from a monotone counter, not merely a unique one: a non-monotone allocation lets the active-set floor (`min_active`) be pulled back below a finished build's sequence, re-protecting an already-condemned blob (a leak); this monotone-`build_seq` floor lemma survives in shipped code for precommit-ref reclaim (`Gc::prefixEligible` / the `BuildPrefix` watermark floor in `CasGc.cpp`), even though the blob-protection use case it was built for was replaced.; The per-candidate minimum-active-build watermark mechanism was replaced by precommit-first reachability; the surviving requirement is that build sequence numbers come from a monotone counter.

CAS treats a plan as a hypothesis about how to proceed, not an authority: plans have been wrong in every round (a field placement that silently rebound positional initialisers, a prescribed proof that proved nothing, a step whose own authorization forbade it), so the person executing a plan is expected to notice when it is wrong and say so rather than execute it as written.

Mid-way through the rev.7 disk-lifecycle plan the user ordered a scope cut to a FORGET-only v1: the natural-erasure proof stack (~1500-2000 lines) was excised entirely (erasure is asserted, never machine-proven), documented as spec rev.8 with a 10-item excision list; TLA+ Model 1 (natural-erasure proof) was dropped while Model 2 (lifecycle/FORGET) remained the gating model, and the excision itself removed a net 1095 lines with a clean adversarial review.

E1 (relaxed replay of RefTableState) shipped as KEEP: the un-materialized overlay makes per-transaction scratch copies O(overlay) instead of O(N), reducing replay cost by 22-25% and strengthening the case for E3.

E2 (owned-manifest index for RefTableState) shipped as KEEP achieving flat O(1) BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit (~712-726 ns), at the honest cost of ScratchCopy +13 ns and BM_ReplayHistory regressing to 50,082 ns/row because the index overlay grows along the never-materializing replay tail; E3 was tasked to recover it.

E3 shipped as the simplified variant with no undo journal: `TrustedHistory` apply-mode does in-place mutation with poison-on-throw (replay-only, poison provably contained at all 3 callers), while `Full` keeps the verbatim two-phase copy; this cut BM_ReplayHistory from 50,082 to 1,725.58 ns/row (-96.6%, ~29x) with writer benches flat.
E5 (mutate-in-place-when-uniquely-owned materialize) shipped as KEEP, cutting unique-owner materialize from O(N) to O(overlay) for both COW containers.

The reviewer's (Mikhail) final disposition of the review findings: most "findings" and comments were judged not real or by-design, with a small set treated as genuine and prioritized: (1) GCR-1 rebuild mount-lease interlock — real, add the interlock; (2) `Build::promote` overwrite leak — the most concrete storage leak, fix by failing closed or repointing; (3) lost-ACK idempotency (W-N1/W-N2/J5) — reconcile by reading post-state instead of blindly replaying; (4) J1/J2/J3 writer-lease-is-not-a-fencing-token — add a SIGSTOP/SIGCONT test first, then re-check `mayMutate` immediately before the shard CAS as a short-term mitigation, `writer_epoch`-in-precondition as the longer-term fix; (5) G-N1 persistent clamp — keep fail-closed but add observability/operator escape. RPL-3 was judged safe in practice because the sender cannot remove a part until it receives an ack, which the receiver gives only after a successful write.

Reviewer disposition: the security finding labeled "SEC-2 - no intra-pool authz" in the reviewer's reply (matching the audit's SEC-3, no intra-pool authorization) is accepted as by-design: all bucket-credential holders share the same trust boundary. RPL-2 (ZK/CAS ref divergence on partial commit) is judged not a CAS-specific issue but general ReplicatedMergeTree partial-commit behavior that the project already knows how to resolve (via detached-parts handling). RPL-4 (`to_detached` relink disabled, always streams bytes) is accepted as a possible real performance issue to recheck, believed to use the same mechanics as a normal fetch. RPL-5 (no dedicated CAS integration tests for quorum/SYNC REPLICA/cloneReplica) is accepted as coverage debt comparable to other ClickHouse features, mitigated by all stateless tests passing successfully against a CAS-backed server.

The follow-up triage's "Close As No-Action / By Design" bucket: G-N3 (spurious ABORTED on lost-ACK round CAS) is a false positive because the next GC round reads the already-committed `gc/state`; cross-shard serializability findings (fractured read, read skew, phantoms) are accepted as by-design; and RPL-2 (ZK/CAS ref divergence) should follow ReplicatedMergeTree's existing detached-part/recovery semantics rather than invent CAS-only cross-registry transactionality.
